clue.text: Noble creature with pride beheaded after moving protest

indicators.note: after places the shortened creature behind the protest in the answer

parts.note: a protest march is a demonstration on the move

indicators.note: a head taken off means the first letter of the creature's name is dropped

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions, and a lioness is one of its members

explanation.surface: A lion-like noble loses her head after a protest march gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a titled lady ranking above a countess, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Erecting a barrier round the bend

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting means standing the word upright, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water

explanation.surface: Building a barrier around a river bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the bend is British slang for crazy or insane.

clue.text: King William initially reigned unusually fairly over us

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first part above the second
initially asks for the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A historical comment that King William's reign was unusually fair to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: William II of England was nicknamed Rufus, probably for his ruddy complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus was the byname of the English king William II, son of the Conqueror.

clue.text: Husband takes composer on ship that hangs about the bay

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the composer above the ship

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A husband brings a composer aboard a ship anchored in the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The bay is not water but a horse of reddish-brown colour; its tack hangs about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps and fittings are hung on a horse, such as a bay, to attach it to a cart or plough.

clue.text: Sudden mistake, taking opposite direction in the middle

indicators.text: taking opposite direction in the middle
indicators.note: the compass point at the centre of the word is swapped for the point facing it, south for north

parts.note: an oversight is a mistake made through inattention

explanation.surface: A sudden error causes someone to turn round midway.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight success is a sudden one, achieved seemingly in a single night.

clue.text: Bar serving tipsy poets

indicators.note: being tipsy means unsteady, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bar serves drinks to poets who are getting tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to suit the drinking, but it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to preclude or prohibit someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Almost the only song they'll do for tanners

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: solo means performed alone, the only one
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A singer claims this is the only song they will perform for an audience of tanners.
explanation.walkthrough: Tanners here are people getting a suntan, not leather workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaria are sunrooms or sunbeds where people go to bronze their skin.

clue.text: Toy dog, or boxer

definitions.meaning: a small flat-faced breed in the toy group
short for pugilist, a fighter with fists

explanation.surface: Choosing between a lapdog and a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pug is a small snub-nosed breed and also slang for a prizefighter.

clue.text: True poet — one out for a spin

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A poet is out of the competition, taking a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirl on one foot or toe in ballet is a rapid spin.

clue.text: The spirit behind somebody else's book?

definitions.text: The spirit behind somebody else's book?

parts.words: The spirit behind somebody else's book?
parts.note: reads as a phantom haunting a book, but means the unseen hired author who writes under another's name

explanation.definitionFit: A hired author writes books credited to someone else, staying unseen like a phantom.

clue.text: Holding back agitation by lower — classes

indicators.note: by places the classes beside the agitation

parts.note: D and E are the lowest bands in the British social grading system
ferment is a state of unrest or agitation

explanation.surface: Restraint is shown by the authorities amid unrest among the lower classes.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades people A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so the lowest classes are D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponement means putting something off, a holding back for later.

clue.text: Leisurely movement within unpopular government

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An unpopular government makes slow progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow musical tempo or a piece in that tempo is a leisurely movement of a work.

clue.text: Sort of film partners found austere

parts.note: in bridge, West and East are partners at the table
stern means strict and austere

explanation.surface: A couple discover a film they watched was severe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy picture set in the American frontier is a genre of film.

clue.text: Craft carrying king and queen, perhaps, in glory

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for adoration

parts.note: to glory, praise and adore is to worship
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a queen is one example of a chessman

explanation.surface: A vessel carries a royal couple in splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' and 'and' are link words; the queen is a chess piece, a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft is skill in making things, the quality of a maker's handiwork.

clue.text: Fitting arrangement of walk-on parts

parts.note: reads as theatre casting of minor roles, but means pieces of wood fitted together into a floor to tread on

explanation.definitionFit: Wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern make a floor, a fitted surface people walk on.

clue.text: Birds cornered, unable to move at first

definitions.meaning: black crows that nest in colonies

definitions.text: cornered, unable to move at first
definitions.meaning: chess pieces that start the game in the corners and cannot move until others clear the way

explanation.surface: Birds trapped in a corner, frozen at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crow-like bird and the chess castle that begins in a corner square.

clue.text: Learning late in life? This may change after work

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone taking up study late in life may find it changes their work.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare word means taking up study late, education begun in old age.

clue.text: Drunken girl at bar in European naval base

indicators.note: drunken means staggering, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy young woman at a bar in a port town.
explanation.definitionFit: The British territory at the tip of Spain has long hosted a Royal Navy station.

clue.text: Heavyweight protecting female songwriter

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ballast is heavy material carried to steady a ship
Di is a woman's name, standing for any female

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer protects a female songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of ballads, simple narrative songs, is a kind of songwriter.

clue.text: Plant bird dropped in German river

indicators.note: dropped in means put inside, so the bird goes into the river

parts.note: the Mosel is a river in western Germany
a chat is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A plant and a bird fall into a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: Moschatel is a small woodland flowering plant, also called town-hall clock.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman took cover before gaol-break

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: hid means concealed oneself, took cover

indicators.note: a break here means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman hid himself before escaping from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower nobility in Spain.

clue.text: Front part of trunk or box

definitions.meaning: the front of the human torso
a large container with a lid

explanation.surface: Describing the front of a tree trunk or a box.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the thorax at the front of the body and a sturdy storage container.

clue.text: Gull with splendid cage

parts.note: to gull is to dupe or con someone
fine means excellent or splendid

explanation.surface: A seagull in a splendid birdcage.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage something is to shut it in and restrict it.

clue.text: Itinerant friend of Pythias put back in charge

indicators.note: put back means turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: Damon and Pythias are the legendary pair of loyal friends from Greek tradition

explanation.surface: A wandering friend of Pythias is returned to his post.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant means travelling from place to place, a wandering way of life.

clue.text: Split a dried flower-bud

definitions.meaning: the past tense of cleave, meaning split apart
the dried bud used as a spice

explanation.surface: Splitting open a dried flower bud.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the past tense of cleave and the spice made from a dried bud.

clue.text: Recall a source of relaxation — like a sleeper, perhaps

parts.note: to recall a decree is to annul or revoke it

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Remembering something that once helped you unwind, like sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper is a small ring worn in a pierced ear to stop the hole closing, not a sleeping person.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped, as a sleeper earring is.

clue.text: Working everyone up, that's plain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: on means functioning, working
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Keeping everyone busy is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy plain in South America.

clue.text: He left religious books in this lodging-place

indicators.note: in puts the books inside the other pieces

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: A man left his bibles behind in a guest house.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a building providing lodging for travellers.

clue.text: Start one drink and hold forth about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the speaking verb wraps the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to hold forth, speak at length
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink and starts lecturing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or start something.

clue.text: It's a very long time, as Scotsman said

indicators.note: said tells us the name is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman remarks on what a long time it has been.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period of time, an age.

clue.text: Settle quietly, always

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
ay is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Settling a matter quietly, as one always does.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay a bill is to settle it.

clue.text: Highly elated, like the nursery cow

definitions.meaning: the cow in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle jumped this way

explanation.surface: Delight compared to a cow from a children's rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means delighted, and the rhyme's cow jumped above the lunar orb.
